title: Shared Mailbox Triage & Routing Guide
summary: How the Customer Services, Repairs and Rents & Income shared mailboxes are checked, categorised, prioritised and routed, including safeguarding, Awaab's Law, phishing and fraud escalation rules.
author: P030

blocks.p: Our three shared mailboxes are often the first contact a resident, partner or supplier has with {{company.fictional_name}}. Emails that are missed or sit in the wrong place have led to complaints, Ombudsman findings and, in the worst cases, risk to residents. This guide sets out who checks each mailbox, how every email is **categorised**, **prioritised** and **routed**, the response times we commit to, and the red flags that must be dealt with before anything else.

It applies to contact centre advisers, repairs planners, income officers, their cover, and anyone building a Copilot agent, Outlook rule or Power Automate flow that reads these mailboxes. Every email must end up with **one category, one priority and one owner**, recorded in Keystone (or FieldLoop for repairs).

bullets: Mailboxes are checked at **08:30, 12:00 and 16:30** on working days. The Monday 08:30 check covers everything that arrived over the weekend.

The mailboxes are **not monitored out of hours**. The auto-acknowledgement tells senders to phone for emergencies (gas: 0800 111 999; repairs and Careline out of hours: 01622 900 100; danger to life: 999).
Emails that arrive after the 16:30 check are not seen until the next morning, so the 08:30 check must start with a **red-flag scan** of everything received overnight.

numbered: **Scan for red flags first** (section 6): gas, danger to life, a resident not seen, domestic abuse or safeguarding, damp and mould affecting a child or vulnerable person, phishing and bank-detail changes. Read the **whole** email - disclosures are often buried in the middle of a routine rent or repair query.
**Categorise** using one of the categories in Table 2. If an email raises two issues, triage the more serious one and create a second task for the other.
**Prioritise** using Table 3. Vulnerability, children, older residents living alone and repeat contact all move an email up.
**Check history** in Keystone and FieldLoop: is there an open complaint, damp case, repair job or arrears action? Add to the existing case rather than opening a new one.
**Route** to the owner in Table 4 and record the owner and due date. Move the email to the 'Actioned' folder.
**Reply or acknowledge** only if this mailbox owns the response. Never reply to phishing, fraud or media emails.

bullets: **Gas smell:** phone the resident immediately. Tell them not to use switches or flames, to open windows, turn off the gas at the meter if safe, leave the home and call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. Then raise an emergency job. Never just reply by email.
**Water near electrics, sparking, burning smell:** Emergency priority, whatever the original job says. If a job has been logged at the wrong priority, change it and tell the planner.

**A resident not seen or not answering**, especially an older person living alone: Critical. Contact the SilverLiving Coordinator or Careline for an immediate welfare check; if there is no answer, follow the forced-entry procedure and call 999.
Read every email in full. A disclosure is often in the middle of a rent query or repair chaser.

Route domestic abuse disclosures the same day to the domestic abuse lead and the safeguarding lead. Do not reply with details of the disclosure, do not send letters to the address if the resident says the perpetrator reads post, and update the contact preference.
Pause arrears escalation and home visits until the domestic abuse lead has completed a risk assessment.
Forward safeguarding emails only to the named leads. Do not paste them into Teams chats, other documents or Copilot prompts outside the pilot's approved agent.
Every damp, mould or condensation report is a Damp & mould email, even if the resident says 'not urgent'. Never reply with 'open your windows' advice alone.

**Emergency hazard** - for example extensive mould in a room where a baby, a person with a respiratory condition or an older resident sleeps: Critical. The home must be made safe within 24 hours (treatment, temporary room or decant).
**Significant hazard:** investigate within 10 working days, send the written summary within 3 working days of the investigation, and start safety works within 5 working days.
Check for previous damp cases at the address. A recurrence after treatment is a sign the cause wasn't fixed and should be escalated to the Head of Repairs.
Damp reported through a complaint, a councillor or MP, a TSM survey or an operative still needs a damp case to be opened - a complaint on its own does not start the investigation.

blocks.h2: 7.4 Complaints, the Ombudsman and elected members

bullets: If a resident says they will go to the Housing Ombudsman or their MP, treat it as High. Contact them within 1 working day and remind them of their right to go to the Ombudsman. Never discourage it.
Always check Keystone for an open complaint and add new contacts to it.
Any email from a resident whose account is at NOSP served, court action or possession stage goes to the Income Manager the same day.
**Breathing Space** (Debt Respite Scheme) notifications are statutory. Record the moratorium the same day and stop all enforcement and arrears contact for the debt. Ongoing rent remains due.
Long leaseholders are not served a NOSP for rent arrears; their service charge arrears are recovered under the lease.

Warning signs: urgency or threats ('suspension tomorrow'), links asking you to sign in, a sender domain that is close to but not the same as the real one, no named sender, attachments you didn't expect.

Our genuine suppliers' domains are in the contracts register; check the domain character by character. For example, Keystone Software emails come from keystonesoftware.co.uk and Weald Roofing from wealdroofing.co.uk.
**Phishing:** don't click, reply or forward to colleagues. Use the Outlook Report phishing button, tell IT the same day, then delete.

**Bank-detail changes:** never act on an email. Finance verifies by phoning the supplier on the number already held in Northway Finance Cloud, not the number in the email, and holds payments until confirmed. Treat any bank-detail change sent to a non-finance mailbox as suspicious.
Never send an auto-reply or acknowledgement to a suspected fraudster - it confirms the mailbox is live.

blocks.p: During the Copilot pilot, staff may use Copilot in Outlook to summarise and suggest a category, priority and owner for shared-mailbox emails. The person checking the mailbox remains responsible for the triage decision.

bullets: Copilot suggestions must be checked against this guide. A one-line summary can miss a buried disclosure, so read flagged emails in full.
Automated flows may **apply categories, move information-only mail and post alerts** that show the mailbox, time and category only - never the content of the email.
Automated flows must **not** reply to, forward or summarise safeguarding emails, act on bank-detail changes, click links, send replies to media, complainants or data requests, or close repair jobs.
Where a model's confidence is low, leave the email uncategorised for a person.
Triage logs and test sets should use email IDs and tenancy references only, not vulnerability details.

blocks.p: The Customer Service Team Leader samples 20 triaged emails a month for accuracy and timeliness and reports to the Director of Customer Experience. Missed red flags are logged as learning and reviewed at the weekly complaints case review.
